title: AI Made Your Easy Work Free. That Made You More Valuable.
why_read: An opinion piece arguing that AI commoditizing routine coding work increases the relative value of judgment and architecture skills, a common but reasonably argued take.
analysis: The article argues AI has made the 'easy,' well-documented parts of software development, like boilerplate CRUD code and standard UI patterns, essentially free to produce. It claims this shifts the real value of engineers toward things AI doesn't do well, like judgment, architectural decisions, and handling ambiguous or novel problems. This is a reasonable and increasingly common argument in the current discourse about AI's effect on software careers, but it doesn't bring new data, research, or a particularly novel framing. Useful as a think-piece for career perspective rather than as technical content.
